finalists.label: Erysipeloid
finalists.why: The patient's occupation and contact with animals, along with the appearance of vesiculobullous lesions, support this diagnosis.

finalists.label: Cellulitis
finalists.why: The evolving lesions on the left hand and the presence of hemorrhagic bullous lesions are consistent with this condition.

finalists.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
finalists.why: The extension of the lesion to the palm and ventral aspect of the thumb with an eroded area and pustules is characteristic of this disease.

finalists.label: Cutaneous anthrax
finalists.why: Although there is no direct evidence, the patient's contact with animals could potentially support this diagnosis.

frontier_selector.why: The combination of the patient's occupation, contact with animals, and the specific appearance and evolution of the lesions on the hand make Erysipeloid the most likely diagnosis, despite the negative PCR result for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae.
